I'm one of the composers, but a young one who is still trying to carve a niche for himself. I'm heading to a conservatory after the summer to begin studying composition and orchestral conducting, and the above question is making me worry very much about this decision. Part of me thinks that a composer should keep the audience in mind while still doing everything possible to create original work, but my teachers have always drilled it into my head that I should only write down what I want to (this way of thinking may very well be part of the problem, although I can see why composers think this way).

On the other hand, there are just as many people who might like the masterpieces of the previous centuries, but have a passionate distaste for modern compositions. This one upsets me, as beautifully crafted, current classical music (not even just classical... jazz/rock/rap/electronic/insert genre of choice here) that can be easily found if one looks for it. I feel as if there is a terrible stereotype on it that it all sounds of bowed cymbals, guttural strings and pianos being smashed (Part of this is definitely the fact that this style of music is more frequently promoted by classical music authorities, be it from festivals or publishers or record labels). The same type of thing that comes from people who say they hate country or they hate rap. There's always a few songs that make people go "yeah that was pretty good".

So who is it? Which group can sooner make a bigger impact? Mixture of both?
Q: Is general dislike of contemporary classical music the fault of the composers or the listeners?

That's a tough question! But both sides are right. The bottom line is that there are more bad audiences than there are bad artists. Artists usually put out what they want to portray. Bad audiences disparage works for not being what they want them to be, even if they weren't intended to be that. I'd say that you gotta do what you love doing. Accept critique that understands what you're trying to do and reacts to exactly that. And ignore critique from people that note that you're putting out a perfect bowl of tomato soup, but they're interested in vichyssoise, so you get a 2 out of 10. Only accept critique from tomato soup aficionados!

That's a very interesting take on it, thank you! in a conversation with one of my jazz friends he says something similar about how because of the scope and complexity of musical genres in current times, only a few characteristics stick with a genre, and those characteristics are what, in general, the genre is defined as. He says he loves it when he tells people to come to his jazz show, just to have the same people come up to him afterwards and ask if it was jazz or not!

Yeah, totally! And I've seen this with my gf when eating out or even when going out to see a show. She loves soup, so we'll hit a restaurant that's famous for their chicken soup. But she'll complain that it's no good because she loves creamy chicken soup and not brothy chicken soup. But brothy soup is just as legitimate as creamy soup! It's just a personal choice, and she needs to recognize that. Plus we see a lot of acts that do both blues and country music. She loves the blues but is kinda 'meh' about country. So when her favorite acts do more country than blues, she's disappointed and thinks the evening was lame. But it's legitimately good country music! Even really good country music. She's just not an objective judge because she wants it to be something that it isn't intended to be. That's gotta be tough for a composer like yourself, but I'm sure it's also a good lesson. Good luck!

Hard to answer this one. But I wouldn't say that its the composers majorly. At a certain time, Bach and Mozart to name a few were loved by many people and were considered mainstream. The type of music appealed to most audiences and to some, it just wasn't of their musical taste. New music was released and people tended to move towards that if influenced by those around them or the general public creates a 'necessity' for people to "like this music or you have a shit taste in music". I'm sure you know where I'm coming from.

I'm not a musician but an avid music lover and I realise that some composers compose for the current audience/style of music and some don't care and people treat that genre or style of music as alternative/indie. I never hear anyone talk about contemporary classical music or at least jazz and blues unless they play an instrument or simply enjoy that type of music (I have relatives who are like this). Music is crap nowadays anyway and I think that if there was a new wave of classical music or rather, music with 'actual instruments', that it could become the next best thing.

It really depends on how the music sounds. The general public are always busy doing things and need something to keep them active and alert. Which is why I guess up-beat music and loud tones are generally more accepted by the public nowadays rather than classical music which puts you to sleep or helps put you into a relaxed state of mind. If you could mix contemporary classical music and the upbeat tones of modern pop music, maybe this generation will like it.

It's the listeners. There's a niche for everything. If somebody wanted to make music that the most amount of people would enjoy then they would make pop music. I feel like the reason why is a combination of a lot of factors. Taste is the obvious one, but one nobody mentions is social stigma towards listening to classical music.

I am no expert on classical music, so I won't try answer your question. But I do want to ask you a question: Do you think that movie, tv, and game scores count? I hear a lot of music I would consider as classical in each.

I may be biased since I also score films, but I consider them to count. However, I know of a lot of people who don't. Film, television, and game composers all use classical techniques in their orchestrations. The argument on the other side is that these composers incorporate world music and popular styles in their scores, which for some is enough to see it as not classical (Which is bullshit, since classical composers like Copland and Bernstein incorporated Jazz into their symphonies, which would've been pop music when they were writing). I see this as a strength, personally.
OP, what contemporary classical composers would you recommend?
Post-vacation recommendation list incoming: Robert Aldridge, John Adams, and Liebermann are the three I always show people that ask this question.

This is a great question and one that I have never thought of before, and when I do think about it I know that I would rather go to see a performance of Vivaldi, for instance, than any contemporary composer. So in this case it is my fault for possessing a negative bias towards modern composers. I feel that nothing written lately can even come close to my favorite classical pieces, and after searching around for years and finding nothing I have reaffirmed that bias in my mind.

In my opinion no one will ever be as good as The Greats; I feel the same way about art as well. I guess I just idolize the past...

But may it be the case that this is true; that nothing acousto-phonetically pleasing as, let's say RV215, has been produced in many hundreds of years. In this case it would be the fault of the composers.

I think the answer really lies in the culture of the times. This music is losing popularity within each subsequent generation, and many children that would otherwise have gone on to be great composers are no longer towards such things as options, or are never presented with such options to begin with.

I would say it is the modern culture that is pushing people away from classical music in general.

It is the fault of the listeners. Most people don't appreciate classical music. If you compose with those people in mind, you will gain more of their support, but lose support from the members of your audience that enjoy your specific style.

I raised hell as a child. In the first grade, I got my first swats in school for writing "Fuck" on the front door. I would've got away with it if not for that girl. The rest of my early years were more or less the same.

In high school I really had it going on. I went to a very small school, only 11 in my senior class, 2 of which were exchange students. The few girls in my class were always on my nuts. They did my homework or whatever else I needed. I only ever fucked one of them, and I was madly in love with her, still am. I dipped snuff in all my classes, nobody cared. The Ag teacher bummed dips from me on a regular basis. On the weekends there would always be a crowd at the church parking lot drinking beer. The local cop would come by and make sure we weren't causing trouble. He was a nice old man. I now live next to his mother, and she makes me miss that old fucker. I miss those days...

So I made it through high school, didn't have much of a plan. Had every chance to go to college but I didn't (huge mistake, go to school guys). I ended up going to a trade school where I learned to weld. Now, I grew up on a farm, so I knew how weld. They taught me to weld pipe, which is totally different and blew my mind at first. Turns out, pipe welders are in short supply here in the states. After 8 months in school I was making money hand over fist. I was 19 years old and was making thousands every week. As far as I was concerned, I was king shit. I bought fancy tools, ate at fancy restaurants, fucked fancy hookers, you name it and it was fancy shit. By now I'm sure you can see where this is headed.

Now for the shitty part. So I was off on the west coast working, getting rich and all that. One night, my traveling partner and I go to the bowling alley to sip some beers and wind down from work. He had a fake ID, I never needed one, maybe it was my charm? We'll never know. Anyway, we meet some ladies and I ended up leaving with one. Yada yada, you know what happens. I get back to the motel late, and maybe get 2 or 3 hours of sleep. I get up early the next morning, get my buddy up, and we head to work. So I'm driving us to work, I'm not driving very fast because of all the damn moose on the road. I fall asleep, and hit another car head on. My buddy is fine, he's flipping his lid trying to get us out of these cars. He manages to get me out of the pickup and I can't move for the pain. The car I hit? An older couple off on a trip of some sort. The woman didn't make it, but the husband did. He was in pretty bad shape, but he made it. My injuries are irrelevant.

So fast forward, and I'm looking at some prison time. I ended up taking a plea bargain. 26 months in prison for Vehicular Homicide. At my sentencing, the man and his family were there. The judge first asked the family if they had anything to say. By this point we knew each other well. They stood up, every one of them, and cursed me for their mother's death, but took up for me. I will never understand why they did this. Then when my time came, I poured my heart out to those people. I felt absolutely awful, I didn't want to be alive, didn't think I deserved to be. There wasn't much I could say to them, except I'm sorry. I made a bad choice, and this is what happened. They accepted my apology, and I'll never understand how they could do that.

So I go to prison. I'd still be there if not for my mother. I have the best mother in the world. Fuck your mom, mine is better. It was scary, but after awhile I wanted to stay there. Again, my mother bless her soul. While I was there, I sent and received many letters from the victims family. I'm not going into detail so don't ask. I read book after book after book. It was boring as fuck there, but I tried to better myself as best I could.

When I got out of prison, my mother drove all the way across the country to pick me up and bring me home. I didn't want to be there. I wanted to die. I wanted to trade places with her. I was lost. I didn't know what to do. I spent a few years living with mom and dad, not doing much. Helping out on the farm here and there. I quit drinking. Not a drop. But it caught up to me. That thought in the back of my mind, "you're an awful piece of shit". I started drinking again, and I couldn't stop.

I finally got it together. I'd already done so much to disapoint my mother, I couldn't stand to do it to her anymore. I went and got a job driving a truck in the oilfield. I've always loved trucks, fucking loved them, but trucking wasn't my dream job. It's mostly the stigma attached to it. But I did it, and I stuck with it. I made enough to buy a house and move out of mom's house. I kept at it, I worked 100 hours a week, which is illegal as fuck. You can't drive a truck that many hours, but I did it, and still do.

Now I've made enough that I've bought my own truck. I drive for myself, and I make a pretty good living at it. I work my ass off every single day. If I'm not driving, I'm working on the truck so I can keep driving it.

This isn't how I wanted my life to be at all. My past haunts me every single fucking day, it's hard to live with. Sometimes I just want to end it. The only reason I'm still kicking is because I want my mother to be proud of me, and she absolutely is. I've got a good woman that I grew up with on my side now, and I'm just keeping on keeping on. The struggle is real yall. Go to school, tell your parents you love them, and live each day like it's your last.

It's about making complete game from scratch on C-like C++.
Start with something super simple, like a cookie clicker clone, and google specific things that you need to do right now ("unity add button", etc). Or that's how I learned at least.

After you do the first three then go through the UI tutorial because that will be a major aspect of almost any project you work on.

I haven't done the roguelike tutorial yet.

RB Whitaker did a bunch of great tutorials on XNA, which is now no longer developed but the Monogame project is a mostly compatible open source version. He has tutorials for both, and the XNA specific ones should still work with Monogame. I found his C# Player's Guide book to be very helpful as well, though it's focused more on the basics of programming rather than specifically on games.
